A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NUCFL research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original NUCFL experiments, including accuracy and calibration measurements, baseline comparisons, sensitivity tests and a reversed-weighting ablation.

after.justification: V3 reports revised and additional original experiments, including repeated-seed benchmark results, further optimizer comparisons and additional robustness tests.

M1.justification: The calibration objective, DCA/MDCA losses, similarity measures and similarity-based weighting in Equation 8 remain unchanged. New Algorithm 2 documents the existing integration procedure. The CIFAR-100 backbone replacement concerns the experimental setup rather than a new NUCFL component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification using MNIST, FEMNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. V1 already includes centralized training, heterogeneous partitions and partial participation. V3's additional partition and participation configurations extend settings within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated comparisons involving FedSpeed, FedSAM, FedMR and FedCross in Table 25, and CCVR and FedLC in Table 27. FedCal was already evaluated in v1. Conversely, Focal loss results for FedDyn and FedNova on CIFAR-10 at alpha = 0.1 disappear from the corresponding comparison: v1 Table 13 versus v3 Table 17.

E3.justification: CIFAR-100 experiments change from AlexNet to ResNet-34, including centralized training. V3 also adds a 100-client, 10%-participation configuration, local-epoch settings of 1 and 10, and additional FEMNIST/CIFAR-100 partition configurations. The standard 100 rounds, five local epochs and 20-bin calibration metrics remain.

E4.justification: V3 incrementally extends existing robustness analyses with more severe partial participation across partitions (Table 24), adds local-epoch sensitivity testing (Table 26), and adds a FEMNIST reliability case (Figure 7). The reversed-weighting ablation remains, while the main sensitivity plot changes from MNIST to CIFAR-100.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without seed counts or variability estimates. V3 states that experiments use four random seeds and supplies means and standard deviations throughout Tables 7–22. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting; it does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Results change extensively across retained comparisons, and substantial new result entries appear. For example, Table 1's CIFAR-100 FedAvg NUCFL(DCA+L-CKA) accuracy/ECE changes from 73.73/5.14 to 62.05/6.14 alongside the backbone replacement, so this is not a same-setting deterioration. V3 additionally reports broader centralized results, further partition results, new optimizer evaluations and an MDCA-based NUCFL-plus-temperature-scaling result.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, calibration definitions and similarity-weighting formulation remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; both explicitly characterize the contribution as empirical.

C1.justification: The principal calibration, accuracy-preservation and compatibility claims remain. However, Remark 1 replaces v1's categorical claim to be the first work addressing model calibration specifically for FL with an early-work claim concerning calibration across FL algorithms, a limited qualification of novelty.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.6 distinguishes calibration-method and FL-optimizer accuracy–reliability trade-offs. Appendix B.5 acknowledges that partial participation can make the previous global model unrepresentative of the full distribution. The conclusion also identifies personalized and unsupervised FL extensions, refining applicability without changing the central mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: V3 adds explicit NUCFL integration pseudocode in Algorithm 2 and settings for newly evaluated methods, including FedSpeed's lambda = 0.1, FedCross's alpha = 0.99 and FedLC's tau = 1. Existing optimizer details, batch size and V100 hardware disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for ResNet, FedSpeed, FedSAM, FedMR and FedCross, and qualifies the priority statement in Remark 1. Appendix B.7 expands the positioning against the already-cited CCVR/FedLC literature through empirical comparisons. The main related-work organization and distinction between confidence calibration and accuracy-oriented calibration remain.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. V3 makes localized paragraph revisions, clarifies confidence versus calibration and automatic weighting, expands appendix navigation with B.5–B.7, and updates author and publication-header text. These changes do not constitute a wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V3 adopts the ICLR layout, places both principal benchmark tables together, and restructures appendix tables into stacked optimizer groups accommodating uncertainty estimates. Centralized and FedCal tables gain additional column groups, further reliability diagrams appear, and Algorithm 2 is added. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses an important empirical-reporting gap by supplying four-seed means and standard deviations where v1 provided no run variability. Comparisons with six additional FL optimizers and further participation and local-epoch tests substantially strengthen assessment of NUCFL's claimed applicability. Algorithm 2 improves procedural clarity. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including Appendix B.6's misattribution of plain MDCA FedDyn results to NUCFL. The changed backbone means revised scores alone do not demonstrate improvement.
